critical_code_review_comments: Two-source-of-truth risk: the customer app talks to Supabase directly for menu, while the backend exposes /api/menu that also reads Supabase-then-Mongo. If any client (kiosk? loyalty app?) uses /api/menu while pizzadenfert.fr uses Supabase directly, divergence during Supabase outages is possible. Pick one contract.

The Supabase anon publishable key is embedded in shipped web bundles (safe by design), but the current RLS policy set gives that key read-all on menu_items and NO write. This is the correct posture for public-facing reads. Write-path must go through an authenticated admin session (Supabase Auth) OR through a server-side proxy that holds the service_role key. Right now /admin-cms tries the former but with credentials that don't exist in Supabase — worst of both worlds.
